message.content:
Search the codebase for all server-side enforcement of memo visibility (access control, permissions checking, authorization for who can view a memo). Look for:
1. API endpoints that return memo data with authorization checks
2. GraphQL resolvers with memo permission logic
3. Database queries with visibility filters
4. Any other server surfaces that enforce who can view memos

For each enforcement site found, identify:
- The file path
- The function/resolver name
- What type of enforcement it is (REST endpoint, GraphQL resolver, database layer, etc.)

Return a comprehensive list of all distinct enforcement sites (there should be at least 3).

Turns any input (code, docs, papers, images, videos) into a persistent knowledge graph with god nodes, community detection, and query/path/explain tools.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. 1	package v1
2	
3	import (
4		"context"
5		"errors"
6	
7		"github.com/usememos/memos/internal/profile"
8		"github.com/usememos/memos/server/auth"
9		"github.com/usememos/memos/store"
10	)
11	
12	// ErrUnauthenticated is returned by the Authorizer when a request must be rejected
13	// for lack of valid credentials. Each transport maps it to its own status code
14	// (Connect: CodeUnauthenticated, gRPC-Gateway: HTTP 401).
15	var ErrUnauthenticated = errors.New("authentication required")
16	
17	// Authorizer is the single source of truth for method-level access control.
18	//
19	// It authenticates a request from its Authorization header and decides whether the
20	// (possibly anonymous) caller may reach a given RPC procedure. The Connect
21	// interceptor and the gRPC-Gateway middleware share one Authorizer so both
22	// transports enforce identical rules.
23	//
24	// Role-based authorization (admin checks) stays in the service layer; this type
25	// governs only authentication and anonymous access.
26	type Authorizer struct {
27		authenticator *auth.Authenticator
28		store         *store.Store
29		profile       *profile.Profile
30	}
31	
32	// NewAuthorizer creates an Authorizer backed by the given store, token secret, and
33	// instance profile.
34	func NewAuthorizer(store *store.Store, secret string, profile *profile.Profile) *Authorizer {
35		return &Authorizer{
36			authenticator: auth.NewAuthenticator(store, secret),
37			store:         store,
38			profile:       profile,
39		}
40	}
41	
42	// Authenticate resolves the caller from the Authorization header, returning nil for
43	// an anonymous request. It never enforces policy — pair it with CheckAccess.
44	func (a *Authorizer) Authenticate(ctx context.Context, authHeader string) *auth.AuthResult {
45		return a.authenticator.Authenticate(ctx, authHeader)
46	}
47	
48	// CheckAccess enforces method-level access policy for procedure given the
49	// authentication result (nil = anonymous). It returns nil when the request is
50	// permitted and ErrUnauthenticated otherwise.
51	//
52	// Policy:
53	//   - Authenticated caller (access token or PAT): always permitted here.
54	//   - Anonymous + protected method: denied.
55	//   - Anonymous + public method, open instance: permitted.
56	//   - Anonymous + public method, private instance (no InstanceURL): permitted only
57	//     for the auth-bootstrap set, plus CreateUser during first-run setup.
58	func (a *Authorizer) CheckAccess(ctx context.Context, procedure string, result *auth.AuthResult) error {
59		if result != nil {
60			return nil
61		}
62		if !IsPublicMethod(procedure) {
63			return ErrUnauthenticated
64		}
65		if a.profile.AllowAnonymous() || a.allowedOnPrivateInstance(ctx, procedure) {
66			return nil
67		}
68		return ErrUnauthenticated
69	}
70	
71	// allowedOnPrivateInstance reports whether an anonymous request to a public
72	// procedure is still permitted while the instance is private. It allows the
73	// auth-bootstrap set, plus CreateUser while the instance has no users yet
74	// (first-run admin setup).
75	func (a *Authorizer) allowedOnPrivateInstance(ctx context.Context, procedure string) bool {
76		if IsAuthBootstrapMethod(procedure) {
77			return true
78		}
79		if procedure == createUserProcedure {
80			return a.noUsersExist(ctx)
81		}
82		return false
83	}
84	
85	// noUsersExist reports whether the instance has no users yet (fresh install).
86	func (a *Authorizer) noUsersExist(ctx context.Context) bool {
87		limitOne := 1
88		users, err := a.store.ListUsers(ctx, &store.FindUser{Limit: &limitOne})
89		return err == nil && len(users) == 0
90	}

11	func (*APIV1Service) parseMemoOrderBy(orderBy string, memoFind *store.FindMemo) error {
12		if strings.TrimSpace(orderBy) == "" {
13			return errors.New("empty order_by")
14		}
15	
16		// Split by comma to support multiple sort fields per AIP-132.
17		fields := strings.Split(orderBy, ",")
18	
19		// Track if we've seen pinned field.
20		hasPinned := false
21		hasExplicitTimeField := false
22	
23		for _, field := range fields {
24			parts := strings.Fields(strings.TrimSpace(field))
25			if len(parts) == 0 {
26				continue
27			}
28	
29			fieldName := parts[0]
30			fieldDirection := "desc" // default per AIP-132 (we use desc as default for time fields)
31			if len(parts) > 1 {
32				fieldDirection = strings.ToLower(parts[1])
33				if fieldDirection != "asc" && fieldDirection != "desc" {
34					return errors.Errorf("invalid order direction: %s, must be 'asc' or 'desc'", parts[1])
35				}
36			}
37	
38			switch fieldName {
39			case "pinned":
40				hasPinned = true
41				memoFind.OrderByPinned = true
42				// Note: pinned is always DESC (true first) regardless of direction specified.
43			case "create_time", "name":
44				// Only set if this is the first time field we encounter.
45				if !hasExplicitTimeField {
46					memoFind.OrderByTimeAsc = fieldDirection == "asc"
47				}
48				hasExplicitTimeField = true
49			case "update_time":
50				// Only set if this is the first time field we encounter.
51				if !hasExplicitTimeField {
52					memoFind.OrderByUpdatedTs = true
53					memoFind.OrderByTimeAsc = fieldDirection == "asc"
54				}
55				hasExplicitTimeField = true
56			default:
57				return errors.Errorf("unsupported order field: %s, supported fields are: pinned, create_time, update_time, name", fieldName)
58			}
59		}
60	
61		// If only pinned was specified, still need to set a default time ordering.
62		if hasPinned && !memoFind.OrderByUpdatedTs && len(fields) == 1 {
63			memoFind.OrderByTimeAsc = false // default to desc
64		}
65	
66		return nil
67	}
